title: fix(storage)!: a record write claims or copies only a file its caller may read
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DM7SePpQnQZ7NUSKUCvUrek)_

Fixes #25692

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none

## What changes

ADR-0104 D3 (wave 2) gives each `sys_file` at most one owning field slot. A record write that references a file id either claims an unclaimed file for the writing slot, or, when another slot owns the file, copies its bytes into a fresh `sys_file` the writing slot owns (copy-on-claim). Neither step asked whether the write's caller may read the file. The claim path now asks the download door's own verdict, under the write's caller context, and claims or copies only on an allow.

- **One judgement, two callers.** The door's verdict body moves out of `buildFileReadAuthorizer` into `judgeFileRead`: the uploader, a reader of the record whose field owns the file (`readableFieldOwners`, honouring `fileAccessDelegate`), a member of the organization for a file no record owns (#25693), a reader of any `sys_attachment` parent for an attachments-scope file. The download door calls it with no change in behaviour. The claim path calls it through `buildFileReferenceReadAuthorizer`, which also admits a `public_read` file and asks nothing on a kernel with no `auth` service, where the door binds no gate either. One file has one access rule, decided in one place.
- **The quiet answer, after #25682.** A file the caller may not read is answered exactly as the organization-scoped lookup answers a file it cannot see: the id is kept as written, and nothing is claimed or copied. This follows the precedent #25682 set for the cross-organization half of the same lifecycle. There is no new error code or status, and the write cannot tell "may not read" from "does not exist".
- **Ordering.** Constraint verdicts no longer run ahead of the read check.
- **A write's own copy.** A copy the write itself minted is claimed by that same write without a second question. The mint is remembered per write (keyed on the write's dispatch scope). When that record is missing, the write fails safe: the copy stays unclaimed and is never claimed for the wrong caller.
- **Outage.** An authorization-store outage (`AuthzStoreUnavailableError`) fails the write with its declared envelope rather than reading as either answer. Any other throw from the judgement is a deny.
- **Unchanged.** System writes and context-less programmatic writes carry no caller to ask, and reference files as before.

`callerContext` (attachment-access hooks) is exported so the lifecycle reads a write's caller the same way, with operation-private keys dropped. The system-context page (`content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`) gains row 47f for the claim path's system-write exemption, which `check-system-context-census` requires.

## BREAKING, shipped as `patch`

The changeset carries Before / Now / Fix and the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: no spec key, stored row or exported declaration moves. A write that referenced a file its caller may not read now keeps the id unowned. To fix, reference the file as a caller who may read it, or upload it again. A server-side process that copies files between records on purpose runs as a system write.

## Tests

- `file-reference-lifecycle.test.ts`: 15 new cases against a stand-in verdict. They cover refusal on insert and update for owned files (no copy) and unclaimed files (no claim, a tombstone not revived), per-id judging of a multiple-value field, the constraint ordering with its control, the verdict being asked with the caller context (operation-private keys dropped), outage propagation (the record is not written), and system, context-less and unbound writes unchanged. Controls show an admitted caller still copies and claims.
- `file-reference-read-verdict.integration.test.ts` (new): 11 cases on a real ObjectQL and SqlDriver with `StorageServicePlugin` booted. For each file, the download door's answer to the writer and the claim path's outcome for the same writer agree. A refused file gets 403 and is kept; a served file gets 200 and is copied or claimed. The cases span the field-owned, delegate, attachments, uploader, `public_read` and unclaimed arms, plus outage and other-fault pins and a system write.
- Package suite: 65 files, 1179 tests pass. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` compiles both files.

## Ablations

Every negative pin was put back to the refused behaviour and shown red, then restored. Each leg ran through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: the anchor hit 1 → 0, the blob changed, the restored blob equals HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` was empty.

| Leg | Mutation | Red |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | the lookup ignores the verdict | 15: every unit refusal, ordering, caller-context and outage pin, and every integration refusal and fault pin. Every integration allow control stays green. |
| B | the lifecycle swallows a verdict throw | 2: the unit and integration outage pins |
| C | the plugin's binding admits everyone | 5: the integration refusal and fault pins |
| D | the plugin's binding stops re-raising an outage | 1: the integration outage envelope pin |
| E | a write's own copy is asked again | 1: the unit control "claimed without a second question" |
| F | a system write is asked | 1: the unit system-write pin |

## Gates

All on head `4f3c21e5`. The service-storage closure was built first, then the whole repo (`pnpm build`, 119/119 tasks).

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derives 102 gates. All 102 exited 0, and `--ran` reconciles them: 102 derived, 102 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
- `pnpm lint` (repo-wide `eslint . --no-inline-config`): exit 0.
- `check:commit-card-trailers --range origin/main..HEAD`: all 6 commits carry the model-free trailer pair.
- Dogfood battery (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test`, no shard, no path, under the verify lock): 295 of 299 files passed and 3 were skipped; 2522 of 2541 tests passed and 18 were skipped. The one failure was `packaged-flow-write-door-parity.dogfood.test.ts`, "a flow no package ships is still created, updated and removed through the same door", which hit its 5 s timeout while the 102 gates ran on the same 4 cores. Re-run alone under the lock: 5/5 passed. The test touches no file field.
